scan.permission: Local network permission was denied. Enable it in system settings and try again.
scan.complete: Checked twelve TCP ports and compatible protocols. A reachable port does not prove a vulnerability. Internet exposure and cloud/P2P access still need separate checks.
web.readable: The browser received a readable HTTP response. This does not identify the model, firmware or security of the device.
web.unknown: The browser cannot determine the result. CORS, local network permission, certificates, mixed content, a timeout or an unreachable device may be responsible. This does not mean the device is absent.
upnp.noResponse: No reply to the targeted UPnP search. This does not prove UPnP is disabled; check the router settings.
upnp.noGateway: A UPnP device responded, but no compatible gateway service was found. UPnP does not necessarily imply port forwarding.
upnp.complete: Read the selected UPnP service’s mapping list. This may exclude manual forwarding, DMZ, PCP/NAT-PMP and IPv6 firewall rules.
upnp.partial: UPnP responded, but the mapping list could not be fully read. Check the router settings.
upnp.limit: Showing the first eight mappings of the selected UPnP service. The list may be incomplete.
upnp.incomplete: UPnP check incomplete: incompatible service, permissions or network error. No settings were changed.
rtsp.unknown: The port is reachable, but RTSP was not confirmed.
rtsp.metadata: The / path responds without credentials and advertises SDP metadata. Check camera authentication. Video access has not been demonstrated.
rtsp.auth: The / path requests authentication or denies access. Other paths and cloud access have not been verified.
rtsp.confirmed: RTSP confirmed; video access could not be determined at /. No images were acquired.
rtsp.incomplete: RTSP check incomplete: timeout, a different protocol or an incompatible response.
onvif.identity: ONVIF product information received. These are self-reported device claims; confirm them on the label.
onvif.auth: The standard ONVIF path requests authentication or denies access; the service has not been conclusively identified.
onvif.unknown: No verified ONVIF identity at the standard path. A camera or different endpoint may still exist.
onvif.incomplete: The standard-path ONVIF check could not be completed.
external.mobileOnly: Use the installed app on a phone connected to cellular data.
external.network: Turn off Wi-Fi and VPN, then enable mobile data. No external check was performed.
external.complete: The system reported cellular connectivity before and after these checks. Routing is not pinned to that interface; repeat if the network changed or a VPN remained active. A reachable port does not identify a router panel or camera. Failed connections do not prove complete isolation: cloud/P2P, IPv6, UDP and other ports remain unchecked.
guide.remote-admin.title: Keep router administration on the trusted network
guide.remote-admin.why: Internet-facing administration increases the attack surface.
guide.remote-admin.action: In router settings, find Remote management, WAN administration or Web access from Internet and disable access you do not need. Restrict administration to trusted devices. Do not blindly disable ISP management services.
guide.remote-admin.verify: Check both IPv4 and IPv6. A LAN test, even against the public IP, cannot prove Internet access is blocked. Use the separate cellular check and confirm the router configuration.
guide.camera-cloud.title: Review who can access your cameras
guide.camera-cloud.why: Cloud and P2P can provide remote access without port forwarding.
guide.camera-cloud.action: In the vendor app, review Remote access, P2P, Cloud, shared users and active sessions. Remove unknown access, enable MFA when available and turn off remote access you do not use. For access from outside, consider a maintained VPN with restricted permissions rather than exposing the camera directly.
guide.camera-cloud.verify: Check the camera, NVR recorder and cloud account separately. Netscan does not sign in to accounts or attempt to view footage.
guide.forwarding.title: Review incoming connections to your home
guide.forwarding.why: A forwarding rule can expose a device to the Internet.
guide.forwarding.action: Find Port forwarding, Virtual server, Port triggering and DMZ host in the router. Remove rules you recognise as unnecessary. Avoid placing a camera or NAS in a DMZ. Review UPnP, PCP/NAT-PMP and IPv6 inbound rules as well.
guide.forwarding.verify: The UPnP list can be partial and does not describe all rules. Changing the port number does not replace access control.
guide.upnp.title: Decide whether you need UPnP
guide.upnp.why: It can let local devices request router port openings.
guide.upnp.action: Disable UPnP if you do not need it. If games or other services require it, regularly review which devices create mappings and restrict it to the networks that need it where supported.
guide.upnp.verify: Repeat the check after making changes. An unanswered SSDP probe does not prove UPnP is disabled.
guide.segments.title: Separate trusted devices, IoT and guests
guide.segments.why: A compromised device should be able to reach as few other devices as possible.
guide.segments.action: Trusted: personal computers and phones. IoT: cameras, TVs, plugs and appliances. Guests: visitors. Use separate networks with firewall rules: IoT and guests should not reach trusted devices or router administration. Allow only necessary paths, such as your phone reaching the recorder. Different Wi-Fi names alone do not ensure isolation.
guide.segments.verify: Test from each network, including IPv6. Casting, printers and hubs may need narrow exceptions. A scan from one network cannot certify segmentation.
guide.legacy.title: Turn off services you do not use
guide.legacy.why: Traditional Telnet and FTP can transmit credentials without encryption.
guide.legacy.action: Review Telnet, FTP, SSH, file sharing and remote desktop in device settings. Disable unused services. Prefer encrypted administration restricted to trusted devices. An open port is a clue: confirm the actual service before changing it.
guide.legacy.verify: Repeat the check after changes. Nonstandard ports and unsupported services can remain undetected.
guide.updates.title: Update devices and check support dates
guide.updates.why: Fixes depend on the exact model, hardware revision and firmware.
guide.updates.action: Use the official vendor app or website, enable automatic updates where available and check the support end date. Follow the vendor’s backup instructions before updating.
guide.updates.verify: Check the installed version afterwards. If support has ended, plan a replacement and restrict connectivity in the meantime.
guide.accounts.title: Protect accounts and shared access
guide.accounts.why: A compromised cloud account can bypass home-network defences.
guide.accounts.action: Use unique passwords for the router, devices and cloud accounts, a password manager and MFA. Remove unused accounts. Never enter passwords into Netscan.
guide.accounts.verify: Review shared users, active sessions, login notifications and recovery methods.
guide.wifi.title: Review Wi-Fi and firewall settings
guide.wifi.why: Encryption and inbound rules protect access to the network.
guide.wifi.action: Use WPA3 where compatible, or at least WPA2 with AES. Avoid WEP and TKIP. Disable WPS if unnecessary, and keep IPv4 and IPv6 firewalls enabled.
guide.wifi.verify: Check these settings in the router. TCP scanning does not measure Wi-Fi encryption or firewall configuration.
guide.recovery.title: Prepare recovery and repeat checks
guide.recovery.why: Security also requires noticing changes and being able to restore devices.
guide.recovery.action: Keep a protected configuration backup, review unfamiliar devices and vendor notices. Before giving away a camera, remove cloud sharing, unlink your account and follow the vendor reset procedure.
guide.recovery.verify: Review settings after adding devices, major updates or router replacement.
app.intro: Clear evidence and practical steps. A scan cannot certify that a device or network is secure.
privacy.title: Privacy
privacy.body: No account, advertising or analytics. Results stay in memory unless you choose to save the inventory on this device. Device backups and clipboard sync are controlled by your operating system. NVD, CISA/GitHub and FIRST receive the public IP and the data described before each optional lookup. Links follow the destination site’s privacy policy. No scan certifies security.
scan.title: Check a device
scan.instructions: Connect to the network’s Wi-Fi. Find device IPs in the router’s device list, or select a discovered device.
scan.browserLimit: The browser may block HTTP or invalid certificates.
scan.authorize: I own this network or have permission to check it.
scan.wait: Checking ports and compatible protocols. This may take about a minute.
scan.invalidIP: Enter a private IPv4 address, for example 192.168.1.1. Find it in your router’s device list.
scan.error: The check could not be completed. Review local network permission and try again.
scan.copied: Report copied. It contains network addresses; share it carefully.
link.error: This device could not open the link.
web.install: Use the installed app for protocol, UPnP and external-access checks.
web.openHint: Install the app first. Opening a link only fills the address; it never starts a scan.
report.identity: Self-reported ONVIF identity: {vendor} {model}, firmware {firmware}. Confirm it before checking advisories.
report.mappingOn: Enabled mapping. Confirm you need it; Internet reachability is not proven.
report.mappingOff: Disabled mapping. Internet reachability is not proven.
report.unknown: Closed, filtered, timed out or blocked by permissions: the state is undetermined.
hint.telnet: Often used by Telnet, which does not encrypt traffic. Confirm the service and disable it if unnecessary.
hint.ftp: Often used by traditional FTP. Check encryption and whether it is needed.
hint.http: Possible HTTP service. This does not prove it is the router panel or Internet-facing.
hint.https: Possible HTTPS service. The port alone does not verify protocol or certificate.
hint.ssh: Often used by SSH. Restrict confirmed administration services to trusted devices.
hint.smb: Possible SMB file sharing. Review need, users and allowed access.
hint.rdp: Possible remote desktop. Review whether it is needed and restrict access.
hint.rtsp: Common streaming port. See the RTSP protocol check.
hint.other: Service not identified. A port number does not identify the manufacturer.
advisory.title: Check security advisories
advisory.instructions: Confirm the manufacturer, exact model, hardware revision and firmware from the label or settings. ONVIF claims need confirmation too.
advisory.allow: Send manufacturer and model to NVD for this search.
advisory.privacy: NIST service in the USA: receives the search text and your public IP. Do not include names, passwords or serial numbers.
advisory.invalid: Enter manufacturer and model, at least three characters.
advisory.error: Search unavailable. NVD may be offline or rate limiting requests. Try again later.
advisory.candidates: Keyword matches are candidates, not confirmed device vulnerabilities. No results does not mean no vulnerabilities.
guide.title: Protect your network, one step at a time
guide.instructions: Guided settings checks. Your confirmations are self-reported, not automated tests or certifications.
external.title: Check from outside your home
external.subtitle: Mobile app + cellular data · separate check
external.instructions: 1. Read the home connection’s dedicated public IPv4 in the router. Do not probe a shared CGNAT address. 2. Turn off phone Wi-Fi and VPN; enable mobile data. 3. Enter the address and run the check. No Netscan account or scanning server is required.
external.authorize: I verified this is my dedicated public IP, have permission to check it, and turned off Wi-Fi and VPN.
external.invalid: Enter your dedicated public IPv4. Private addresses, CGNAT and IPv6 are not supported by this check.
external.error: Check incomplete. Use the mobile app and review cellular data and permissions.
external.copied: Report copied: it contains your public IP.
inventory.intro: Discover advertised services, import existing reports and keep track of changes. Discovery is not a complete network census.
inventory.storagePrivacy: Optional local storage, not encrypted by Netscan. May be included in OS backups. Disable to delete the saved copy.
inventory.storageError: Local storage could not be read or updated. Do not assume your data was saved or deleted.
inventory.empty: No devices yet. Discover services, import a report or enter a device IP.
inventory.groupHint: This label does not configure network isolation.
inventory.clearQuestion: Delete the in-memory inventory and its saved local copy? Exported files and clipboard data are not deleted.
discovery.done: Discovery finished. Devices that do not advertise supported services can remain invisible.
discovery.failed: Discovery could not finish. Check network permission and your Wi-Fi connection. You can still enter an IP.
discovery.web: Native discovery requires the installed app. Import a report or enter an IP to use web light.
import.done: Reports imported locally. Importing never starts network requests.
import.error: Could not import this file. Use Netscan JSON or Nmap XML, up to 2 MB.
import.nmapCoverage: Imported Nmap observations, not a new scan. Only explicitly listed TCP ports and service fingerprints are included; script output and UDP are not imported.
import.untrusted: Imported observations · provenance and accuracy are not independently verified.
delta.warning: Compared only ports checked in both reports. An IP can belong to a different device after DHCP changes.
delta.unreachable: No longer reachable in this check: {ports}
delta.different: Different scan profiles: these reports cannot be directly compared.
match.title: Match an official advisory locally
match.coverage: Reviewed coverage: Archer AX21 (US V1.2/V2/V3), ASUS RT-AX55, two Hikvision models.
match.confirm: I confirmed these product details on the device label and settings.
match.affected: Firmware matches a documented affected version or range
match.outsideKnownRange: Outside this rule’s documented affected range · not a clean bill of health
match.needsDetails: More exact product details are required
match.unsupported: No reviewed local rule for this exact model
match.scope: This is advisory applicability based on the details you confirmed, not an exploit test. Coverage is limited to the named CVE and model. No result certifies the device is secure. Rules reviewed on 12 November 2026.
match.ax21Details: This rule covers US Archer AX21 revisions V1.2, V2 and V3. Enter the full firmware, for example “1.1.3 Build 20221116”, hardware revision and US region. Other regions and formats require manual review.
match.ax21Action: TP-Link’s advisory links firmware separately for V1.2, V2 and V3. Use the matching hardware and region page, or update through Tether/router settings. The rule uses the CVE boundary 1.1.4 Build 20230219; prefer the latest supported vendor firmware rather than assuming that old boundary is the latest release.
match.asusDetails: Confirm the exact RT-AX55 model and firmware string. This conservative rule checks the explicitly documented 3.0.0.4.386_50460 release only.
match.asusAction: TWCERT lists RT-AX55 3.0.0.4.386_50460 and recommends upgrading to 3.0.0.4.386_51948. Check ASUS for the latest supported firmware. Versions not explicitly matched here still need vendor review.
match.hikDetails: This rule covers DS-2CD2122F-I and DS-2CD2022F-I from the documented DS-2CD2xx2F-I family. Use the full format, for example “V5.3.0 build 150513”. Other suffixes, OEM variants and formats are not covered.
match.hikAction: The advisory identifies DS-2CD2xx2F-I versions V5.2.0 build 140721 through V5.4.0 build 160530. Use Hikvision’s model-specific firmware and upgrade instructions; do not cross-flash another hardware/OEM variant. Restrict camera access while checking support.
threat.title: Prioritise with exploitation context
threat.allow: Fetch CISA KEV and FIRST EPSS for these CVE IDs.
threat.privacy: GitHub/CISA receives your public IP when downloading the full catalog. FIRST receives your public IP and these CVE IDs. No inventory, local IPs or firmware are sent.
threat.scope: KEV records observed exploitation; prioritise applicable KEV vulnerabilities. EPSS estimates exploitation activity over the next 30 days across the wider population, not the chance your device will be attacked. Neither proves this device is affected. Failed or missing feeds stay unknown.
threat.kevNo: CISA KEV: not listed in the downloaded catalog
threat.error: Exploitation context could not be retrieved. No low-risk assumption was made.
banner.ssh: SSH protocol greeting received. The banner is self-reported evidence, not proof of patch status.
banner.telnet: Telnet negotiation bytes received. Disable unused Telnet and prefer encrypted administration on trusted networks.
banner.ftp: FTP greeting received. Verify whether encryption is enforced and disable the service if unnecessary.
banner.unknown: No conclusive protocol greeting. Do not identify a service from the port number alone.
